summary: Full backend + frontend validation of Meta Pixels manager, lead deletion (single/bulk), French overseas phone validation, landing visuals, consent-gated Meta Pixel integration and existing regressions. 25/25 pytest backend tests pass. Admin UI (Meta Pixels CRUD + lead delete + bulk delete selection) works. Landing shows LIVRET D'ÉPARGNE heading + eligibility badge. fbq is undefined before consent; after consent, fbevents.js loads and window.__metaPixelEvents records PageView then Lead (pixel_id=1905482920834524) after submitting the 2-step form with a Guadeloupe phone (0690445566).

issues: React a11y warning: Missing Description/aria-describedby on DialogContent (Radix Dialog). Non-blocking but should be fixed by adding DialogDescription.

action_items: Optional: add <DialogDescription> inside pixel-dialog, pixel-delete-dialog and lead-delete-dialog to clear Radix a11y warning.
critical_code_review_comments: admin_routes.update_pixel allows empty body (no-op returns ok:true even if pixel doesn't exist) — minor UX only.
public_routes submit_lead silently returns ok:true on honeypot/fast_submit without flagging, which is intentional (anti-bot) and correct.
/api/pixels/active correctly refuses to fall back to default pixel when an unknown campaign is passed.
seed_data_creation: Tests create and clean up TEST_ pixels. Several Guadeloupe/Martinique/Guyane/Reunion/Mayotte/metropole leads were created via POST /api/leads during phone validation tests (not deleted — flagged as 'doublon' on duplicate submissions). One lead was deleted via the admin UI during the delete flow.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend rate limit is 8/hour per IP in default settings; the pytest session temporarily raises rate_limit_per_hour=1000 and min_submit_seconds=0 via /api/admin/settings and restores at teardown. Email validator requires deliverable domain (DNS MX), so tests use gmail.com addresses. The published form has exactly 2 steps: step1 (birth_date/last_name/first_name/email/phone), step2 (amount cards only — no 'ville' field in current published form). window.__metaPixelEvents is a diagnostic journal exposed by src/metaPixel.js — PageView fires on consent accept, Lead fires on successful submit.
